thread:
morgan: heads-up — noticed a host-side CPU spike in prod after the recent kernel-selector tweak. flamegraphs point to tokenization + transport framing, not GPU time.

jin: saw that too. appears correlated with the new 'prefer-fp16-minibatch' rule that lands a bunch of short requests on a different path.

alex: can you paste the top of the flame? curious if it's our tokenizer or malloc churn.

morgan: flame snippet (top symbols):
```
 42%  tokenize_from_frame
 18%  http2_write_small_frames
 12%  memcpy_simd
  8%  kv_cache_lookup_locked
  6%  parse_request_line
```

sasha: interesting — memcpy_simd up high suggests extra copies when the parser hands chunks to the kernel path. maybe fragmentation increased after kernel switch.

jin: i instrumented sequence-length distribution for a 30m window: 78% <= 64 tokens, 15% 65-256, 7% >256. the new selector is batching those tiny requests differently — it forces prefix-normalization that reallocs into 512B buffers.

morgan: exactly. small requests are getting blown up to 512B buffers and then split into 128B frames for streaming. causes two bad things: extra memcpy + more HTTP2 frames (http2_write_small_frames above).

alex: any evidence KV cache behavior changed? more misses or lock contention?

jin: kv stats during the spike: miss_rate +12%, lock_wait_ms median doubled. looks like we thrash hot entries because of slightly different key normalization (we added a suffix token id in the selector path).

sasha: patch idea: 1) revert aggressive fp16-pref path for <=64 token requests 2) change allocator to use pool for <=128B pre-serialized buffers 3) add prefetch on kv lookup for new conn warmup.

morgan: rough config snippet i prototyped to gate the path by length histogram sampling: 
```
{ "kernel_selector": {
    "prefer_fp16_for": { "min_tokens": 65 },
    "sampling_window_secs": 300,
    "short_request_gate": { "enabled": true, "max_token_length": 64, "sample_rate": 0.05 }
  },
  "allocator": { "small_buffer_pool": { "enabled": true, "size": 128 } },
  "kv": { "conn_warmup_prefetch": 3 }
}
```

jin: note the sample_rate 0.05 is to let us collect performance telemetry without full-scaling the new path for shorts. we can ramp if it's clean.

sasha: i'll try a small write that switches the kernel gate to min_tokens 65 and add the small_buffer_pool on the runtime host. will run canary in us-west-2.

perf-bot: deploy started by sasha — canary: 5 hosts, window: 15m, metrics: cpu_user, http2_small_frame_rate, kv_miss_rate.

morgan: after 10m canary: cpu_user down 28% on canary hosts, http2_small_frame_rate down 40%, kv_miss_rate down 9%. latency p50 unchanged, p95 improved by ~4%.

alex: nice. does this change impact throughput for mid-length requests? need to ensure we're not regressing batch utilization.

jin: quick check: avg tokens/batch for 65-256 bin unchanged within noise. the selector no longer forces them into the fp16-minibatch unless length >=65. good sign.

sasha: i'll promote the patch and open a short postmortem doc. next follow-ups: add automated histogram-driven gates (so selector learns thresholds), add pooled allocator to node image by default, and fix the kv key normalization regression to avoid thrashing.

morgan: thanks — saved a nice chunk of host CPU. leaving notes in the perf board.

perf-bot: deploy succeeded: 5/5 canary hosts healthy. monitoring for 30m. :thumbsup:
